newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia dlr extends offshore slide to fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: Australia dlr extends offshore slide to fresh lows.

text.p: The Australian dollar extended its offshore retreat at the midsession to be almost 3/4 cent down from Friday and at fresh 18-month lows.

Traders were seeing distressed selling from investors who went long in local time Friday when the currency had been up testing US$0.7450. They were caught out badly, therefore, when a gang of U.S. investment banks sold aggressively in New York, swamping key support at US$0.7410.
"The scale of the selloff surprised," said one. "There was good buying all the way down but the offers soaked it all up -- people aren't even waiting for a bounce to sell now."

By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the currency was under pressure at US$0.7378/83 having briefly sunk as far as US$0.7373/78, its lowest level since January 1996. It had opened at US$0.7400/05 after tumbling from US$0.7445/50 late here on Friday.
Dealers reported some exporter bids beneath US$0.7380 but doubted they would do more than delay the currency's descent given the weight advantage of the U.S. and Swiss sellers.

Chart watchers were just as negative about the break of US$0.7410 and expected support levels at US$0.7370 and US$0.7350 to be mere pit stops on the road to US$0.7305, which was last year's low and a major target for bears.

Some suspected the downtrend, which has already lasted four months and cost the dollar six cents, could stretch even further. In particular, they had the 1995 low of US$0.7070 in mind if the dollar failed to recover US$0.7440 soon.

The weakness extended to most of the crosses, except a few like the German mark and Thai baht which had fundamental troubles of their own, and dragged the trade weighted index down to 56.6 from 56.9 late Friday.
The dollar was off at 83.84/94 yen from 84.67/77 but firmer on the mark at 1.3137/49 from 1.3059/70 late here Friday.
